scenes.say: Great setups mean nothing if a losing streak wipes you out. Here's how ICT protects his account.

scenes.title: Size from risk, not hope
scenes.say: Every position starts with risk, not with a target. Decide what percent you'll risk, measure the distance to your stop, and size the position so a stop-out costs exactly that amount.

scenes.title: Only 30% is in play
scenes.say: ICT adds a twist: only allocate thirty percent of your equity to trading. A ten-thousand-dollar account trades as if it were three thousand. One percent of that is thirty dollars. No margin calls, and cash in reserve.

scenes.title: The halving rule
scenes.say: Now the key rule. After a loss, the next trade uses half the risk. Lose one percent, and the next trade risks half a percent. With half risk, a two-to-one winner gets you back to even, and a three-to-one puts you at a new high.

scenes.title: Why it works
scenes.say: Why does it work? Three losses at full size cost three percent. With halving they cost one and three quarters. Smaller size also makes it much harder to revenge trade. Many traders, and this app's tilt guard, also stop for the day after three losses.
points: Losses shrink as the streak grows
You can't revenge-trade at full size
Stop for the day after three losses

scenes.title: Let the app help
scenes.say: The app does this math for you. The position-size tool in Tools applies the thirty percent rule and the halving rule, and the tilt guard reads your journal to tell you today's risk.

els.sub: Position size with the 30% and halving rules · today's risk from your journal

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.say: Protect the account first. Trade only thirty percent of it, risk a small fixed percent, and halve it after each loss. You'll still be here when the good setups come.

els.sub: 30% allocation · 1% risk · halve after each loss
